newsitem.title: CHILE: Chile shares end soft, market weighs earnings.
newsitem.headline: Chile shares end soft, market weighs earnings.

text.p: Chilean blue chips closed lower on Friday in strong trade with the bolsa seen volatile next week as investors focus on company first quarter earnings and U.S. economic data, said traders.
"I expect a downward bias with much depending on the tone of the U.S.," said one broker.
The bolsa is seen continuing to fluctuate in a trading range of 114-119 points, he added.
The 40-share index closed off 0.66 percent at 117.1 points. The general index declined 0.26 percent to 5,324.48 points.
Turnover rose to 16.3 billion pesos from 11 billion pesos Thursday.
Traders noted that company results, which must be published by month-end, have already been factored into stock prices.
"There are unlikely to be any big moves after earnings have been released," said one dealer.

Losers included power giant Endesa which retreated as investors considered its first quarter earnings announced Thursday disappointing, even though they were in line with analysts' forecasts, they said.
"Strong non-operating earnings disguised the effect of the drought on operating income," said one dealer.

Fertilizer-maker Soquimich resumed its losing streak following a downgrade from ING Barings to sell from buy. The analysts cited fears of a profit-squeeze as the result of lower prices in the Chilean market.
Soquimich A stock ended down 2.6 percent at 2,240 pesos.
